newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI bringing in GDR funds gradually.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI bringing in GDR funds gradually.

text.p: Funds raised through a recent overseas equity issue by the State Bank of India will be brought into the country in small lots to avoid affecting the rupee's exchange rate, a top bank official said.

SBI chairman Pandurang Kakodkar said if all the $369.95 million raised through an issue of global depositary receipts early this month were brought into India at once, it would have undesirable repercussions on the dollar-rupee exchange rate.
"If you bring in all the money in one day, it will affect the exchange rate," Kakodkar said.
SBI was also timing the flow of these funds to match the outward remittances of its corporate clients, he said. Kakodkar said part of the funds had already been brought in.
"It (the entire funds raised overseas) will come within a month," he added.
The inter-bank foreign exchange market has been characterised by poor demand for the dollar and abundant supply, leading to upward pressure on the rupee.
The Reserve Bank of India has been buying dollars at the 35.60 level in recent weeks to arrest the rupee's rise.
The dollar was quoted at 35.61/62 rupees in recent deals.
